findings.title: Final deliverable reinstates an unconditional confounding map
findings.evidence: Step 4 at line 22 explicitly says a purely descriptive question need not acquire a causal diagram; line 29 nevertheless requires an evidence table/design packet with a bias and confounding map without an applicability qualifier. The candidate newly introduces the descriptive exemption but leaves the old completion list unchanged.
findings.consequence: A consumer following the completion list can still add causal/confounding paperwork to a descriptive appraisal, defeating the refined branch boundary. This is an instruction-scope conflict, not evidence of a lost scientific control or measured runtime failure.
findings.repair: Qualify the final confounding-map requirement to causal or adjusted associative claims; retain bias/validity review appropriate to descriptive designs and preserve the causal branch's causes/mediators/colliders/selection checks. Change only the entrypoint sentence; no supporting resource needs repair.
findings.followUpCheck: Read/apply a descriptive prevalence-estimate appraisal and confirm sampling, measurement, missingness and uncertainty are inspected without requiring a causal/confounding diagram; separately inspect a causal/adjusted association request to confirm the map remains required. Proposed follow-up, not executed here.

findings.title: Trace field still says capped delay after provider-minimum correction
findings.evidence: The refined step 2 forbids shortening a valid provider wait and defers/exhausts when it exceeds policy/budget. The unchanged evidence list still calls the trace field capped delay.
findings.consequence: The receipt vocabulary may suggest a clipped provider delay even though the operative step correctly forbids early redispatch. It does not override the more specific step, so this is non-blocking.
findings.repair: Describe actual scheduled wait/delay disposition and identify any client-generated backoff cap separately; keep the existing minimum-wait, monotonic budget and cancellation rules.
findings.followUpCheck: Inspect a provider hint longer than the client policy ceiling: the outcome should defer/exhaust with no early attempt and the receipt should distinguish the requested minimum from any backoff cap. Proposed follow-up, not executed here.

findings.title: Discovery description remains narrower than the bounded joint-candidate branch
findings.evidence: Description says one bounded parameter change, while step 1 explicitly permits coupled parameters or a declared optimization step with attribution to the joint candidate. The old body already admitted several parameters; this is a carryover discovery ambiguity made more visible by the refinement.
findings.consequence: A coupled-parameter iteration may be overlooked before the otherwise correct body is read. It is not a weakened solver or attribution check.
findings.repair: If changing the description, refer to one bounded candidate change or bounded parameter iteration while retaining solved-baseline, solver, constraint and accept/rollback semantic cues. Do not alter protected skill.json triggers or invocation policy for this note.
findings.followUpCheck: Compare direct single-parameter and declared coupled-candidate requests against description/body fit; preserve same-solver evidence, hard constraints and joint attribution. Proposed follow-up, not executed here.

limits: Independent of Volta's authorship, but reviewer A authored cohort A and shares the host instructions, plan and author-assessment context; this is not blinded/raw-agent evaluation.

READY means no blocking document finding within this bounded review. REPAIR means an open important or critical instruction defect. Minor findings are recorded even when non-blocking; none is silently repaired.

All 38 complete candidate entrypoints, all 28 declared supporting reference bodies, author dispositions/cases and changed entrypoint hunks were inspected. Retained entrypoints and all supporting files were compared byte-for-byte to the immutable baseline; unchanged byte identity avoids inventing a regression.

Author assessment cases were reviewed as proposals, not executed outcomes. The two fixed consumer tasks are recorded separately in consumer-A-v1.json; they are forward applications, not randomized baseline/candidate comparisons.
No domain solver, workbook/document engine, private corpus, live service, clinical/legal decision, campaign, GPU/HPC job, game/audio runtime, research participant or production target was exercised.
No catalogs were built, product files edited, tests/full suite run, integration/release/install performed, external material acquired, or other agent/model/provider used.
Existing external documentation links were not fetched or freshly qualified; relevant local mechanism/resource consistency was the review boundary.

Historical method receipt/report bytes and directory bindings were checked for identity, not re-adjudicated as new domain or runtime certification. Existing DRAFT, instruction-reviewed and not-performance-qualified meanings remain distinct.
Token, cost and timing-performance counters are unavailable. No efficiency or runtime-superiority claim is made.
Parent retains discovery/package verification, confirmed repairs routed to their author, integration and release decisions.
